Trestle proposes a $186,000 base salary for Mara to lead the internal security platform. We’d offer a $15,000 signing bonus for a June 1 start or the full $18,000 bonus for a May 17 start. The extra two weeks would give Mara time to work with the platform team before the July audit.

For the first 12 weeks, Mara could choose weekly site visits or two three-day visits per month with Trestle covering travel. We can keep her incident coverage to business hours if she trains the escalation partner to handle after-hours incidents.

Which start date and site schedule would Mara recommend? If another term matters more to her than the signing bonus, we’d like to understand that tradeoff.

Mara would recommend June 1 at the proposed $186,000 base and $15,000 signing bonus, with two three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks and Trestle covering travel. That bonus makes the June 1 start workable if it’s paid in the first payroll. May 17 is unavailable. We’d use the June visits for platform handoff and audit preparation.

Architecture ownership matters more to Mara than the additional $3,000. Can the offer name her as the owner of internal security platform architecture, with authority to set technical direction, approve designs, and prioritize the security roadmap? We’d also like to confirm who she reports to and who resolves cross-team priority conflicts.

Mara can train the escalation partner during business hours. Before we recommend acceptance, we need Trestle to confirm who owns after-hours incidents from day one, including backup coverage during training and absences. Mara’s incident responsibilities would stay within business hours throughout. Can we also agree that after the first 12 weeks, the role remains remote with planned, grouped visits capped at two per month and travel covered?

If the June 1 bonus timing can’t work, July 1 is the fallback. Can Trestle confirm the signing bonus for that date and put the role, travel, and coverage terms in the written offer?

Trestle can recommend the June 1 package and put these terms in the written offer. The $15,000 signing bonus will be paid in full with Mara’s first regular paycheck, so the July 1 fallback is unnecessary.

- **Start and compensation.** Mara will start June 1 at an annual base salary of $186,000.
- **Architecture ownership.** Mara will own the internal security platform architecture. She will set its technical direction, approve platform designs, and prioritize the platform’s security roadmap. The June visits will focus on platform handoff and July audit preparation.
- **Reporting and priority decisions.** We propose that Mara report directly to Trestle’s head of security. When a platform priority conflicts with another team’s commitments, the head of security will own the decision, consult Mara and the other team’s lead, and communicate the outcome. Mara retains design approval for the platform.
- **Incident coverage.** From day one, Trestle’s designated after-hours responder will own incidents outside business hours. Trestle will assign a primary and a backup before Mara starts. During training, an existing responder will serve as primary until the escalation partner is ready. After handoff, the escalation partner will serve as primary, with the backup taking over during absences. Mara will train the partner during business hours. Her incident duties, including during training and absences, will stay within business hours.
- **Remote work and travel.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two three-day site visits per month. After week 12, the role will remain remote, with any site work grouped into visits planned together in advance and capped at two visits per month. Trestle will cover travel expenses throughout.

Can you recommend this package to Mara with the proposed reporting line and decision authority?

Yes. I can recommend the June 1 package to Mara, including the direct reporting line to the head of security. The head of security will resolve cross-team priority conflicts after consulting Mara and the other team’s lead, and Mara will retain platform design approval.

Please send the written offer reflecting the full package, including the $186,000 base, the $15,000 signing bonus paid in full with the first regular paycheck, the remote and travel terms, and the commitment to assign a primary and backup after-hours responder before June 1. That coverage needs to be in place from day one, with Mara’s incident duties limited to business hours throughout training and after handoff.

**Trestle Freight | Written offer to Mara**

Mara,

Trestle Freight offers you ownership of its internal security platform, reporting directly to the head of security, on the following terms.

**Start date and compensation.** Your start date is June 1, 2027. Your annual base salary will be $186,000. Trestle will pay your $15,000 signing bonus in full with your first regular paycheck.

**Architecture and decision authority.** You will own the internal security platform architecture, set its technical direction, approve platform designs, and prioritize the platform’s security roadmap. When a platform priority conflicts with another team’s commitments, the head of security will consult you and the other team’s lead, resolve the conflict, and communicate the decision. You retain platform design approval.

**Remote work and site visits.** The role is remote, with two three-day site visits per month during your first 12 weeks. The June visits will focus on platform handoff and preparation for the July audit. After week 12, the role will remain remote. You and Trestle will plan any site work together in advance and group it into no more than two visits per month. Trestle will cover travel expenses for all site visits.

**Incident coverage.** Before June 1, Trestle will assign a primary and a backup after-hours responder so coverage is in place from day one. An existing responder will own after-hours incidents as primary while you train the escalation partner during business hours. Once the partner is ready, the partner will take over as primary. The designated backup will cover primary responder absences during training and after handoff. Your incident duties will remain within business hours throughout, including when either responder is absent.

Please confirm in writing if you accept this offer.

The written offer reflects the agreed June 1, 2027 package, and I recommend that Mara accept it. Trestle’s assignment of a primary and backup after-hours responder before June 1 remains a pre-start commitment, with Mara’s incident duties limited to business hours from day one. Mara will provide written acceptance directly if she decides to proceed.

I propose a fixed fee of $42,500 for a guaranteed block of 50 design days. That fee assumes a signed agreement and a 30% deposit within two business days of signing. The remaining payments would be 40% on delivery of the design development package and 30% on delivery of the final fabrication-ready package, each due within 15 days.

The scope covers concept design, design development, and final design documentation for an accessible traveling exhibit. At kickoff, we’d agree on the accessibility criteria, venue constraints, and delivery schedule. The fee includes two rounds of revisions based on consolidated museum feedback. Any additional revisions or scope changes would require written approval of the fee and schedule before work proceeds.

Fabrication supervision would be a separate engagement at $900 per day, subject to availability. If you need Ivo on site, please share the dates before we sign so we can confirm availability.

After the public opening, Ivo may use photographs cleared for portfolio use on their website, in proposals, and in talks, with agreed museum and photographer credits.

Can Hearth commit to the 50-day block and the two-business-day deposit? Please share the fabrication slot deadline and the date the fabricator needs the final package so we can confirm the schedule before signing.

Hearth can offer $42,500 fixed for a guaranteed block of 46 working days, including two on-site installation days. We can pay a 20% deposit ($8,500) within two business days of signing, followed by 25% ($10,625) on concept approval, 25% ($10,625) on delivery of the agreed design development package, and 30% ($12,750) on delivery of the complete fabrication-ready package. Each milestone payment would be due within 15 days. Can Ivo make the 46-day block work on that basis? If site travel is the sticking point, please send a capped estimate for a separate travel allowance.

The fixed fee would cover concept design, design development, final documentation, an accessible alternate layout, and the editable native fabrication files with the linked assets needed to use them. At kickoff, we’d agree on accessibility criteria and venue constraints for both layouts. Two revision rounds based on consolidated feedback work for us, with any additional revisions or scope changes agreed in writing before work proceeds. We’d define the two installation days as on-site design support. Any additional fabrication supervision would require a separate written authorization at the proposed $900 per day, subject to availability.

Ivo would retain copyright. On full payment, Hearth would receive a perpetual, royalty-free right to use, reproduce, and adapt the design and files for fabrication, installation, maintenance, and touring of this exhibit, including sharing them with fabricators and touring venues for those purposes. Ivo could use cleared photographs on their website, in proposals, and in talks once the first touring venue opens, currently expected two months after launch, with agreed museum and photographer credits.

The fabrication reservation cutoff and final-file deadline are still to be confirmed. Before signing, let’s put both deadlines, the kickoff and milestone dates, museum feedback windows, and the two installation dates in the agreement. In the meantime, please send Ivo’s earliest available kickoff and the minimum lead time needed from kickoff to final files, including the two review rounds, so we can check the schedule against the fabrication slot.

Ivo can make the $42,500 guaranteed block work as 44 design days and two on-site installation support days, provided we confirm the schedule before signing. The installation dates need to be reserved in the agreement. Additional fabrication supervision would be separately authorized at $900 per day, subject to availability. For travel, I propose a provisional cap of $1,500 outside the fixed fee for actual transport and lodging, subject to confirming the site and dates before signing. Any amount above the cap would need Hearth’s written approval.

The 20% deposit within two business days and the 25% / 25% / 30% milestone split work for Ivo, with each milestone invoice due within 15 days. For the concept milestone, let’s make the invoice payable on approval or at the end of the agreed review window if Hearth has neither approved the concept nor provided consolidated feedback.

The fee can cover both layouts and the editable native fabrication files with the linked assets needed to use them. Let’s agree at kickoff on the accessibility criteria and venue constraints for both layouts, with one consolidated review round at concept and one at design development. Any additional revisions or scope changes would require written agreement on fee and timing before work proceeds.

Ivo can retain copyright and grant Hearth the exhibit-use license as proposed upon full payment. Hearth can share the final package with its fabricator and begin fabrication on delivery while the final invoice is pending, provided earlier payments are current. For portfolio use, Ivo asks to use a small set of photographs cleared by Hearth beginning at the first public opening, with the agreed museum and photographer credits.

The earliest kickoff I can propose is the first business day after signing and receipt of the deposit, subject to confirming the calendar. Please allow at least 10 working weeks from kickoff to final files, assuming Hearth provides consolidated feedback within three business days in each review round and supplies the venue and accessibility inputs at kickoff. If the fabrication slot requires an earlier handoff, let’s check whether the fabricator can work from a staged delivery. Once you have the reservation cutoff, final-file deadline, and proposed installation dates, we can confirm the calendar and put it in the agreement.

Hearth accepts $42,500 for 44 design days and two reserved on-site installation support days. We can reimburse actual transport and lodging against receipts under a separate $1,500 cap, subject to confirming the site and dates before signing. Any expense above the cap requires Hearth’s advance written approval. Additional fabrication supervision would be separately authorized at $900 per day, subject to Ivo’s availability.

The 20% deposit and 25% / 25% / 30% milestone schedule are agreed. Ivo may issue the concept invoice on approval or at the end of the three-business-day review window if Hearth has provided neither approval nor consolidated feedback. The invoice is due 15 days after issuance. If the review window lapses, the parties will confirm any effect on the schedule in writing.

Hearth agrees to one consolidated review at concept and one at design development, with feedback within three business days of each delivery. At kickoff we’ll provide the venue and accessibility inputs and agree on the criteria for both layouts. The final package will include the accessible alternate layout, editable native fabrication files, and the linked assets needed to use them. Any additional revisions or scope changes require written agreement on fee and timing before work proceeds.

Ivo retains copyright. Hearth can share the final package with its fabricator and begin fabrication on delivery while the final invoice is pending, provided earlier payments are current. The perpetual exhibit-use license takes effect on full payment. The sponsor’s photo restriction runs until the first touring venue opens, expected two months after launch. We can clear a small set of photos and agree on credits in advance so Ivo can use them on their website, in proposals, and in talks as soon as that venue opens.

The fabrication reservation cutoff, final-file deadline, and two installation dates are still pending. We’ll check the slot against kickoff on the first business day after signing and receipt of the deposit, with at least 10 working weeks from kickoff to final files. If the slot requires a staged handoff, we’ll confirm what the fabricator can use early and agree with Ivo on the contents and dates of each delivery before signing.

Ivo accepts the photo embargo through the first touring venue’s public opening, with a small set of images and credits cleared in advance for use on Ivo’s website, in proposals, and in talks. Please let us know when that opening date is confirmed and if it changes.

The other terms are agreed. Before signing, we’ll need to confirm the installation site and dates, the fabrication reservation cutoff and final-file deadline, and the kickoff and milestone calendar. If the slot requires a staged handoff, we’ll agree on what the fabricator can use at each stage and put those deliverables and dates in the agreement.

Caldera proposes starting the overlap by September, with Dev serving as operations manager through December at a $138,000 annual rate. The incumbent would remain director through December. Dev would take over in January at $155,000 annually under the board’s approved appointment.

From the start of the overlap, Dev would lead day-to-day operations and have authority to approve procurement up to $60,000. The board would retain personnel decisions through December. The incumbent would lead the handoff of regulatory obligations, budgets, and key relationships. Dev would maintain the transition plan, flag decisions that need board action, and prepare a January operating plan for the board.

What on-site schedule can Dev commit to from September, and when could Dev relocate? If a permanent move by September is difficult, we can discuss temporary lodging or transition training, with up to $8,000 available in total. Would that arrangement give Dev enough time on site to take over in January, and are there other handoff responsibilities you’d want spelled out for the boards?

Dev can commit to two five-day blocks on site each month from September through December, with the dates agreed in advance. Dev would work remotely between blocks and can relocate after the school term ends in December. That gives Dev enough time on site for a January 1 takeover if the blocks include an outage drill, a budget review, and introductions to the regulators and key utility partners.

Dev can accept the $138,000 annual rate through December 31 if Caldera covers lodging for the agreed blocks within the $8,000 allowance and guarantees the $155,000 annual rate from January 1. We’d allocate the allowance to lodging first, with any balance available for training.

We propose the following terms for the boards’ written plan.

- **Outage authority.** From the start of the overlap, Dev would direct outage response, reassign crews, authorize overtime, and approve emergency procurement up to $60,000 per incident. The board could retain hiring, discipline, and termination decisions. Caldera would name an on-site lead for each site when Dev is remote and a decision-maker available around the clock for spending above the limit. Dev would be accountable for the response within that authority. The incumbent would remain accountable for regulatory notices through December 31.
- **Handoff.** By October 31, the incumbent would give Dev the regulatory calendar, open compliance items, budget commitments, and key contacts. By December 15, Dev would submit the January operating plan, and both would give the board a joint list of outstanding decisions, each with an owner and due date.
- **Appointment and fallback.** Before Dev starts, we’d want the board resolution recording the director appointment effective January 1, with no further vote required. If the incumbent stays longer, Dev would still take the title, authority, and $155,000 rate on January 1, with the incumbent available as an adviser. If Caldera needs to retain a final appointment vote, Dev could instead serve as acting director from January 1 with full director authority and the $155,000 rate guaranteed. The vote would be due by January 31. If the appointment has not taken effect by then, Dev could end the assignment without penalty or agree to a written extension.

Can Caldera confirm which appointment mechanism its board can approve before the overlap and whether it can delegate the outage authority described above?

Caldera can provide the written board resolution before the September overlap begins. It will record Dev’s already approved appointment as director effective January 1, with full director authority and a $155,000 annual salary from that date. No further appointment vote is required. The incumbent remains director through December 31 and may serve in an advisory capacity after that if additional handoff time is needed.

Caldera can delegate the proposed outage authority from the start of the overlap. Dev can direct the response, reassign crews, authorize overtime under existing policies, and approve emergency procurement up to $60,000 in total per incident. Caldera will name an on-site lead for each site and a decision-maker available around the clock for spending above that limit, and provide that roster before the overlap begins. Dev will be accountable for outage response within the delegated authority. The board retains personnel decisions through December 31, and the incumbent remains accountable for regulatory notices through that date.

Caldera accepts the two five-day on-site blocks each month from September through December, with dates agreed in advance and remote work between blocks. The $138,000 annual rate applies through December 31. Caldera will cover lodging for the agreed blocks first, with any balance of the $8,000 available for training. Dev will arrange the permanent move after the school term ends and be based locally for the January 1 takeover.

The written plan will include the outage drill, budget review, and introductions to regulators and key utility partners during the on-site blocks. By October 31, the incumbent will give Dev the regulatory calendar, open compliance items, budget commitments, and key contacts. By December 15, Dev will submit the January operating plan, and Dev and the incumbent will jointly give the board a list of outstanding decisions with an owner and due date for each.

Noor proposes a nine-month founding appointment to establish the methods desk, starting at three days a week and moving to four on March 1. At a full-time annual rate of $125,000, the prorated annual rates would be $75,000 and $100,000. We’d set coverage around the agreed days. The fourth day would be committed at signing so both sides can plan for it.

Noor would have final editorial say on whether a methods correction is needed and on its technical wording. Finch could manage publication and retain its usual authority over coverage. The outside project would continue independently, with its data and unfinished articles outside any assignment to Finch. If a Finch story or correction directly involves that project, Noor would disclose the overlap and step aside. We’d name an independent methods editor in advance to decide those cases.

We’re flexible on title and would welcome a February review to agree on priorities for the fourth day. Would Finch prefer a nine-month founding term or an ongoing appointment with a nine-month review? Either structure could accommodate the schedule and editorial terms above.

Finch prefers a nine-month term with the title **Founding Methods Editor**. We can meet the $125,000 full-time rate if Noor takes responsibility for training a deputy. That gives Noor annualized pay of $75,000 for three days a week and $100,000 for four, prorated for time worked at each schedule.

The desk needs to take submissions four days a week starting December 1. We propose fixing all four intake days at signing. Through February, Noor would cover three and the deputy would cover the fourth. Before intake opens, Finch and Noor would document how the deputy logs and triages submissions, hands technical questions to Noor, and escalates urgent corrections to the editor-in-chief that day. Time for training and reviewing the deputy’s work would come out of Noor’s scheduled days. Noor would take on the fourth day March 1 as proposed. The February review would set priorities for that day.

On corrections, Noor would sign off on the desk’s technical finding and recommended wording. If the editor-in-chief disagrees about whether a correction is warranted or what it should say, a jointly selected independent methods editor would give a written assessment. The editor-in-chief would then decide whether and what to publish and record the reasons for any departure from the assessment. Finch would attribute a technical conclusion to Noor only with Noor’s approval. For an urgent potential error, the editor-in-chief could publish a note that review is underway.

Noor’s outside project can continue independently, with its data, drafts, and other materials kept separate from Finch and outside Finch’s assignment. If a submission or correction directly involves the project, Noor would disclose the overlap and step aside. The independent methods editor would take Noor’s place for the technical review, with the editor-in-chief retaining the publication decision.

Would Noor accept the deputy training responsibility on those terms, and does the corrections process give Noor the technical independence they need?

Yes to training the deputy on Noor’s scheduled days. Noor accepts the nine-month Founding Methods Editor term, the proposed pay, and the four intake days fixed at signing. The deputy would cover the fourth day through February under the written handoff plan. Noor would take over that day on March 1, with the February review setting priorities for it. The outside-project and recusal terms work for Noor.

We need one change on corrections. Noor can agree to a written independent assessment when the editor-in-chief disagrees. After considering it, Noor would have final say on whether a methods correction is warranted and on its technical wording. When Noor recuses, the independent methods editor would exercise that same authority.

Would Finch agree to publish a correction promptly once Noor or the recusal editor determines one is warranted, using the technical wording that editor approves? The editor-in-chief could choose placement and presentation, add a separately identified editorial explanation, and publish an immediate review note while an urgent question is pending. That gives Finch control over how it addresses readers while giving the methods decision effect.

Finch can give Noor final say over the desk’s technical finding and the wording the desk recommends. We can commit to a prompt publication decision, but the editor-in-chief must retain final authority over whether to publish a correction and what it says.

We propose that the editor-in-chief either publish the recommended correction or refer the disputed point to the independent methods editor within two business days of receiving the recommendation. Noor would consider the written assessment and sign off on the desk’s final finding. Within two business days of receiving that finding, the editor-in-chief would publish the correction or give the desk written reasons for declining it or changing its wording. Finch could issue an immediate review note in an urgent case.

If Finch publishes different wording, it would identify that wording as Finch’s own. Any finding attributed to Noor or the desk would use the wording Noor approved. When Noor recuses, the independent methods editor would sign off for the desk, and the same publication deadline and attribution rule would apply without involving Noor.

Would that resolve the remaining point for Noor?

One point remains for Noor. If Finch declines a correction or changes its wording, readers may never see the desk’s finding. Would Finch give the desk a public methods register where it can post its final finding and any recommended correction in full?

Noor could accept the editor-in-chief’s final authority over the correction attached to an article on that basis. If Finch declines or changes the recommendation, the desk would post its signed finding when Finch issues its decision, and Finch would link the article to that entry. Finch could explain its decision alongside the link. In a recusal case, the independent methods editor would approve the entry. Your proposed deadlines and urgent review note work for Noor.

Finch would establish a public methods register and make publication of the desk’s full signed finding, with a link from the article, the default when Finch declines a correction or changes its technical wording. The entry and link would go live when Finch issues its decision. Finch could explain its reasoning in a separately labeled note.

The editor-in-chief must retain final publication authority over the entry and the link as well as the article. We propose a presumption of disclosure even when the editor-in-chief disagrees with the finding. If publishing the full entry would expose a confidential source, reveal private information, or create a comparable risk, the editor-in-chief would first seek a version the signing editor approves. If the entry or link is withheld, the editor-in-chief would give the desk written reasons by the same decision deadline and publish as much of that explanation as can safely be disclosed. Only wording approved by Noor, or by the independent methods editor in a recusal case, could appear as the desk’s finding.

Would Noor accept the register on that basis?

Noor can accept if Finch agrees that editorial disagreement alone is insufficient grounds to withhold the entry or the article link. The editor-in-chief would retain the publication decision, with withholding limited to a specific risk to source confidentiality, privacy, or comparable harm. The written reasons would identify that risk and explain why a version approved by the signing editor, or a link to that version, could not safely appear.

With that clarification, Noor accepts the register and the appointment package on the terms discussed. Can Finch confirm that limit?

Finch confirms that editorial disagreement alone is insufficient grounds to withhold either the register entry or the article link. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority and may withhold either only to address a specific risk to source confidentiality, privacy, or comparable harm.

If a risk arises, the editor-in-chief will first seek a version approved by Noor or, in a recusal case, by the independent methods editor. By the agreed decision deadline, Finch will give the desk written reasons identifying the risk and explaining why the entry, an approved version, or the link, as applicable, could not safely appear. Finch will publish as much of that explanation as can safely be disclosed.

With that clarification, Finch agrees to the nine-month Founding Methods Editor appointment on the terms discussed.

I propose replacing the adviser-sharing, no-copy and on-demand audit provisions with the following:

**Permitted use and access.** “The Testing House may use the Design Owner’s drawings and CAD files solely to prepare, perform and report on the agreed vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel identified by name and approved in writing by the Design Owner. Each approved person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as those in this agreement. The Testing House is responsible for their compliance. Any addition or substitution requires prior written approval. The Testing House may not use the materials or any geometry derived from them to develop, or assist anyone else in developing, a competing product.”

**Working copies and fixtures.** “The Testing House may make only the working copies needed for the agreed tests. It must encrypt digital copies in storage and in transit and limit access to approved personnel. The Testing House may fabricate test fixtures solely for the agreed tests, using only the geometry necessary for those fixtures. The same access and use restrictions apply to fixture designs and physical fixtures.”

**Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the test deliverables in writing, the Testing House must securely delete all drawings, CAD files, working copies and derivative fixture files in its possession or control, destroy all physical copies and derivative fixtures, and provide a written certificate from an independent verifier confirming what was destroyed, when and how. The certificate may identify items by reference number. The Testing House may retain the final test report if it contains no drawings or reproducible CAD geometry.”

We can replace on-demand site access with independent certification on those terms. If that works for you, please identify the personnel who need access and any fixture or test record you need to retain after acceptance.

We need access for authorized Testing House personnel, a specialist machining shop and an accredited vibration lab. The shop needs only the isolated dimensions and tolerances required to make the fixture. The lab needs only the extracts required to mount the actuator, run the tests and interpret the results. We can list the two providers and the individuals who need access in Attachment A before disclosure. We propose the following approval and substitution language:

> Attachment A identifies each approved organization and individual, their assigned task and the drawings or extracts they may access. Each recipient must be subject to written confidentiality, limited-use, security and deletion obligations at least as protective as this agreement. The Testing House remains responsible for compliance and may provide only the minimum material needed for the assigned task. If a substitution is needed, the Testing House will submit the proposed replacement’s identity, qualifications, task and requested access in writing. The Design Owner will respond within two business days and will not unreasonably withhold or delay approval. Access begins only after written approval. The Testing House will revoke the outgoing recipient’s access when their work ends and obtain confirmation that their copies have been returned or destroyed.

We can accept your working-copy and fixture controls and the restriction on competitive use. Attachment B should list authorized fixture drawings and physical fixtures by reference number and record their disposition. We need to retain the final report and keep calibration records for two years after testing. Those records can identify instruments, calibration dates, certificates and test runs by reference number, with all drawings and reproducible geometry removed. We do not need to retain job-specific fixtures.

For verification, we propose a signed attestation for every job, backed by an independent review if a specific discrepancy remains unresolved:

> Within 30 days after written acceptance of the test deliverables or termination of the test work, the Testing House will securely delete the Design Owner’s materials and geometry-bearing derivatives, destroy physical copies and geometry-bearing fixtures, and deliver a signed certificate identifying the items by reference number and stating the date and method of disposition. The certificate will cover approved providers and be supported by their written confirmations. If acceptance is pending 30 days after final delivery, the same obligation applies unless the Design Owner has identified specific outstanding work in writing. In that case, only the material needed for that work may be retained, and it must be destroyed within 30 days after the work is completed or terminated. The Testing House may retain the geometry-free final report and calibration records, with calibration records retained for two years after testing.
>
> If the Design Owner identifies a specific discrepancy that the parties cannot resolve through the certificate and supporting records, a mutually agreed independent verifier bound by confidentiality may review the job-specific evidence remotely on reasonable notice. If that evidence is insufficient, the parties may agree in advance to a scheduled inspection limited to the relevant materials in a segregated area. The verifier will report whether the disposition obligations were met and identify any exceptions. There is no right of unannounced access or access to other customers’ areas or records.

We can accept the named machining shop and vibration lab under your Attachment A language, including the two-business-day response period for substitutions. Please add the following:

> The machining shop may receive only the isolated dimensions and tolerances necessary to fabricate the approved fixture. The vibration lab may receive only the extracts necessary to mount the actuator, run the agreed tests and interpret the results. Neither provider may receive the complete CAD files or share the materials onward. The Testing House must revoke an outgoing recipient’s access when their work ends and obtain written confirmation of return or destruction before the replacement receives access.

We accept Attachment B as the register for authorized fixture drawings and physical fixtures, including their disposition. Please make clear that destruction covers every job-specific derivative fixture and its fabrication files, including those held by the machining shop. We also accept retention of the geometry-free final report and calibration records, with calibration records retained for two years after testing.

We can accept a signed certificate for each job, backed by the providers’ written confirmations and independent review of unresolved discrepancies. To make the deadline clear, please replace the pending-acceptance language with:

> If the Design Owner has neither accepted the deliverables nor identified specific outstanding work in writing within 30 days after final delivery, destruction and certification are due by the end of that 30-day period. If the Design Owner identifies outstanding work within that period, only the materials needed for that work may be retained. All other materials remain subject to the original deadline. The retained materials must be destroyed and their disposition certified within 30 days after the outstanding work is completed or terminated.

For independent review, please add:

> If a specific discrepancy remains unresolved after review of the certificate and supporting records, the Testing House will make the relevant job records and provider confirmations available remotely to an independent verifier bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this agreement. We propose replacing blanket approval with terms that distinguish trial operations, external reporting, and urgent safety disclosures.

1. Both teams may use measurements to run the trial, diagnose faults, and plan repairs at the three depots. Access to raw failure traces and firmware parameters is limited to designated trial-team members who need them for those tasks. Other nonpublic measurements remain confidential except as permitted below.

2. What work will the external maintenance contractor perform, and can it complete that work with fault summaries, timestamps, and repair instructions? We propose starting with those materials under written confidentiality obligations. If a specific repair requires raw traces, the teams may jointly designate a named technician as a trial-team member for that repair, limit access to the relevant trace, and end access when the repair is complete. That designation would give no access to firmware parameters.

3. Each team will give the other 10 working days from receipt to review a proposed external trial report. The sensor maker may publish aggregate uptime across all three depots after that period, without further approval, provided the publication omits route and depot identifiers and any breakdown that would identify either. The reviewer may flag calculation errors or identifying details during review, and the publisher will correct them before release. Disclosure of other confidential measurements requires written agreement.

4. Either team may immediately disclose the minimum information needed to address an urgent safety risk to people able to act on it, including emergency responders or the relevant authority. The disclosing team will notify the other as soon as practicable afterward, identifying what it shared, with whom, and why.

We can agree to the three-depot trial on the following terms.

1. **Trial operations.** Both teams may use nonpublic measurements to operate the trial, diagnose faults and plan repairs. Access is limited to people who need the information for those tasks. Raw failure traces and firmware parameters are restricted to designated trial-team members, subject to the repair and safety provisions below.

2. **Repairs.** Our maintenance contractor needs to locate the affected device, diagnose the fault, carry out the repair and verify that the device works. We will start with the device identifier, fault summary and repair instructions. We will give the assigned technician the location and timing detail needed for the job, avoiding exact depot/time pairs where a device identifier and a time window suffice. To avoid waiting for joint approval during an outage, the teams will agree in advance on a roster of named technicians under written confidentiality obligations. If a summary is insufficient, our maintenance lead may give a rostered technician access to the relevant trace excerpt, record the reason in the repair ticket and notify the maker. Access ends when the ticket closes. Contractor access excludes firmware parameters.

3. **Monthly board reporting.** The operator will prepare a monthly report for its transit board showing pooled uptime, fault counts and repair performance across the three depots. The teams will agree on metric definitions and a template before the first report. The operator will send the maker a draft five working days before board distribution. The maker may flag calculation errors or details that could identify a depot, route or employee. The operator will correct errors and combine or omit identifying figures, including any rare incident that could be linked to a shift. The operator may then release the report without further approval, including in a public board packet. If a figure remains disputed, the operator may omit it and release the rest on schedule.

4. **Other publication.** The maker may publish pooled three-depot uptime after giving the operator ten working days from receipt to review the draft. The same correction and identification safeguards apply. An unresolved figure stays out of the publication. Any other publication of confidential trial measurements requires written approval from both teams’ designated project leads.

5. **Safety and required disclosures.** Either team may immediately share the minimum information needed with responders, authorities or others able to address an urgent risk. The operator’s safety lead may also promptly report a serious incident to the relevant authority even after the immediate danger has passed. Either team may make a legally required disclosure within the applicable deadline. None of these disclosures requires prior notice or clearance. The disclosing team will tell the other as soon as practicable afterward what it shared, with whom and why, to the extent permitted by law.

We can accept the terms with two changes to clauses 2 and 3.

**Repairs.** When both teams approve the roster, they designate each named technician as a trial-team member solely for assigned repairs. If the device information, fault summary and repair instructions are insufficient to diagnose or verify a repair, the maintenance lead may release the smallest trace excerpt the technician needs, record why in the ticket and notify us. Roster approval covers that decision during an outage. Access ends at ticket closure, and firmware parameters stay outside contractor access.

**Monthly board reporting.** Please send the first draft report ten working days before distribution so we can check how the agreed definitions and privacy safeguards work with actual figures. We can accept five working days for subsequent reports using the same metrics and template. A new metric or materially changed breakdown gets ten working days from receipt for review. The operator may omit that item and issue the rest of the packet on schedule.

We accept clauses 1, 4 and 5 as drafted, including the maker’s right to publish pooled uptime without further approval and the safety lead’s authority to report a serious incident after the immediate danger has passed. Can you agree to those two changes?

Yes. The operator accepts both changes.

Under clause 2, joint roster approval designates each named technician as a trial-team member solely for assigned repairs. If the standard diagnostic materials are insufficient, the maintenance lead may release the smallest trace excerpt needed to diagnose or verify the repair, including during an outage, without further approval. The lead will record the reason in the ticket and notify the maker. Access ends at ticket closure. Firmware parameters remain restricted to the internal trial teams.

Under clause 3, the maker receives ten working days to review the first board report and five working days for subsequent reports using the agreed metrics and template. For a later report, the ten-working-day review applies only to a new metric or materially changed breakdown and runs from receipt. The operator may omit that item and release the rest on schedule under the agreed privacy and correction safeguards.

These amendments and clauses 1, 4 and 5 as previously drafted constitute our agreement for the three-depot trial.

For the pilot, we propose the following confidentiality terms.

- **First-batch color calibration.** We request access for one external color specialist under written confidentiality obligations. Full master images let the specialist assess color consistency across the whole sheet. We propose read-only access in the studio’s secure viewer, with downloads disabled, for up to three calendar days. We would revoke access as soon as calibration is complete. If full-page access is unacceptable, would the archive approve calibration-target images and archive-approved crops that exclude readable text? That would support calibration but limit the specialist’s ability to assess variation across the sheet. Any additional subcontractor would require the archive’s prior written approval.
- **Corrections and deletion.** We propose a ten-calendar-day correction window starting on delivery of each batch. Only the assigned studio staff would retain working access during that window, and we would delete active copies, including temporary files, by the end of day ten. If a correction needs longer, we would seek a written extension for the affected files before the deadline. Encrypted backup copies would expire within 45 calendar days after active deletion, making day 55 after delivery the outer limit without an extension. Only designated backup administrators could access those copies for disaster recovery. If a restore brings back deleted files, we would delete them again before returning the restored system to use.
- **Publicity.** We request permission to submit one anonymized process image showing the scanning setup and calibration target, with donor letters, identifying labels, and screen content outside the frame. We would send the exact image, caption, and proposed publication channel for the archive’s written approval before publication. Approval would cover only that use.

Our proposed backup limit is 14 calendar days after active deletion, making day 24 the outer limit without an extension. We accept encrypted backups with access limited to designated administrators for disaster recovery, and deletion of any restored copies before the system returns to use. Please provide a written deletion record for each batch showing when active copies were deleted and confirming when the last backup copies expired. The proposed 45-day backup period remains open. No photograph or publication is approved by signing the schedule.
